task: Close the same unvalidated-dict-as-SQL-columns hazard on the sibling bulk-update route that a prior fix already closed on PUT /segments/{segment_id}

app/api/routers/chapters.py.summary: POST /api/segments/bulk-update now enforces the same SEGMENT_UPDATE_ALLOWED_FIELDS whitelist (character_id, speaker_profile_name, audio_status, text_content) used by PUT /api/segments/{segment_id}, before forwarding req.updates into update_segments_bulk(**updates), which builds f"{k} = ?" SQL from those keys exactly like the already-fixed single-segment path. Unknown fields now 400 rather than being interpolated as raw SQL column names. No new constant was defined — reused SEGMENT_UPDATE_ALLOWED_FIELDS.

flow_impact: No flow/invariant shape change: narrows POST /segments/bulk-update's accepted updates dict to the same four fields PUT /segments/{id} already accepts. The frontend's only caller (api.updateSegmentsBulk, frontend/src/api/index.ts) sends only character_id/speaker_profile_name/audio_status, a strict subset of the whitelist, so no legitimate caller is affected.
tests_added: tests/api/test_api_chapters.py: test_chapter_segments_sync_and_update extended — POST /api/segments/bulk-update with an unexpected extra key (speaker_profile_name + evil_column) now asserts 400 and that no partial update was applied. R1 revert-check performed: removing the whitelist check reproduces the underlying bug directly (sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column: evil_column) before the check is restored.
